outputs.L3:
The method measures an electric current and uses the measured value to calculate a duty command value. During an operating step, switching elements are controlled by comparing the duty command value with a carrier wave. The method then determines whether the operating period should be extended beyond a single cycle of the carrier wave.

When the operating period is extended, switching operations are reduced during the first and last half-cycles of the extended period. During the intermediate portion of the extended operating period, the slope of the carrier wave is modified. The modified carrier wave is then compared with the duty command value to determine the switching states of the switching elements. In this way, the method maintains current control while reducing the number of switching operations.
outputs.L4:
An electric power control method controls power supplied through a switching circuit by measuring an output current and calculating a duty command based on the measured current and a target command value. The duty command represents the desired ratio between an on-state period and an off-state period of a switching element. A controller compares the duty command with a carrier wave, such as a triangular or sawtooth waveform, and generates switching signals according to the comparison result.

The controller also determines whether the operating period associated with the duty command should be extended beyond one carrier-wave cycle. When ordinary pulse-width modulation is sufficient, the switching element is driven using a conventional comparison between the duty command and the carrier wave. When an extended operating period is selected, however, the controller modifies the carrier-wave comparison and the resulting switching behavior so that the commanded power can be delivered with fewer switching transitions.

In particular, switching is suppressed or reduced during the first and last half cycles of the extended operating period. During these boundary intervals, the switching element may be held in a selected on-state or off-state rather than being repeatedly switched in response to every carrier-wave crossing. This avoids short or unnecessary pulses near the beginning and end of the operating period.

During the intermediate portion of the extended period, the controller changes the slope or rate of variation of the carrier wave. The modified carrier wave is then compared with the duty command to establish the appropriate switching timing. Adjusting the carrier-wave slope allows the effective duty ratio over the entire extended period to remain consistent with the command value, even though switching is reduced in the boundary half cycles.

As a result, the method maintains current- or power-command tracking while decreasing the total number of switching operations. The reduced switching activity can lower switching losses, limit heat generation, improve conversion efficiency, and reduce electrical noise without materially compromising the accuracy of the supplied power.
outputs.L5:
## Electric Power

Electric power is one of the most important forms of energy in modern society. It is used to light homes, operate machines, power electronic devices, and support essential services such as hospitals, transportation, and communication systems.

Electricity can be generated from several sources. Traditional power plants often use coal, oil, or natural gas, while renewable sources include sunlight, wind, water, and geothermal energy. Renewable energy is becoming increasingly important because it produces fewer greenhouse gas emissions and can help reduce environmental pollution.

After electricity is generated, it travels through power lines and distribution networks before reaching homes and businesses. Because electrical energy can be dangerous, power systems must be carefully designed and maintained.

Using electric power efficiently is essential. Turning off unused devices, choosing energy-efficient appliances, and investing in renewable technologies can reduce electricity consumption and protect the environment. As technology develops, electric power will continue to play a central role in building a cleaner and more sustainable future.
